subject: Architecture
title: Aboriginal Architecture: The Oldest Builders
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Aboriginal Architecture: The Oldest Builders.

hook.text: Aboriginal Australians have been building structures for at least 40,000 years — the longest record on Earth.

buildup.text: Stone houses, fish traps, and channel systems at Lake Condah predate Stonehenge by thousands of years.

discovery.text: The Budj Bim eel traps are engineered waterways that channel eels into stone pens — aquaculture in stone.

twist.text: Colonial narratives claimed Aboriginal people were nomads who built nothing permanent. Archaeology proved otherwise.

climax.text: Budj Bim became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019 — recognizing one of humanity's oldest engineering feats.

punchline.text: The world's oldest engineers were dismissed as having no architecture at all.

quiz.question: What are the Budj Bim structures in Australia?
options: Ceremonial stone circles for astronomical observation
Engineered waterways that channel eels into stone pens
Underground shelters carved into sandstone cliffs
